title: Escalation Playbook v2 + Known-Issues Sprint — Kickoff Notes & Open Questions (Feb–Mar 2026)

content:
Working doc owned by Support (CS org). Purpose: capture kickoff notes, decisions, open policy questions (esp. SLAs + after-hours + what constitutes an escalation), reviewer list, and a rough outline for the Confluence pages we’ll publish as Escalation Playbook v2 + Known Issues & Workarounds.

Project: “Escalation playbook + known-issues sprint” (4 weeks, Feb–Mar 2026)
Exec sponsor: Jasmine Liu (VP Customer Success)
Program lead: Dev Patel (Dir, Customer Support)
Reliability lead: Sean Gallagher (Dir SRE) / Rafael Mendes (SRE escalation owner)
Docs lead: Elliot Price (Dir Technical Documentation)

Why we’re doing this (problem statement)
- Escalations are inconsistent (what we page, when we declare incident, what fields we collect).
- Customer comms cadence varies by individual and by account; confusion on what we can promise.
- Top repeat themes: timeouts, streaming disconnects, 429s/quota confusion, Dedicated latency spikes/capacity shortfalls, Private SSO/SAML & audit-log issues.
- Support loses time gathering metadata after escalation; Eng loses time asking for basics (request IDs, model/version, region, SDK versions, repro steps).

Kickoff meeting notes (2026-02-05)
Attendees: Dev, Jasmine, Sean, Rafael, Elliot, Owen, Priya, Chris, Rachel, Alex

Agenda
1) Define deliverables + timeline
2) Confirm severity + SLA approach (customer-facing vs internal)
3) Confirm escalation paths/ownership boundaries
4) Known issues catalog: tagging + “safe-to-share” policy
5) Sprint execution: what we’ll actually fix in 2–3 weeks

Key points / decisions captured
- We will ship:
  a) Escalation Playbook v2 in Confluence (Support/CS/SRE sign-off).
  b) Updated Support process docs + Jira template/required fields.
  c) Known Issues & Workarounds catalog (internal) with mirrored excerpts in public help docs where appropriate.
  d) Training session + scenarios + answer key.
- We will standardize language across teams:
  - Use a single matrix mapping (P0–P4) to incident severity (Sev0–Sev3). Note: we need final mapping rules (see Open Questions).
- “Escalation” ≠ “Incident”. Escalation is a request for Eng/SRE engagement; incident is declared when service health / multi-customer impact / core infra degradation is confirmed or strongly suspected.
- Paging hygiene is a constraint. Sean/Rafael asked for strict triggers and a pilot period to tune thresholds.
- Known-issues workarounds must be validated before publishing. No speculative mitigations.

Notes from SRE (Sean/Rafael)
- We need clearer guardrails:
  - When Support can page oncall directly vs go through #eng-escalations triage.
  - What minimum data is required to page (request IDs, timestamps w/ TZ, region, model, SDK version, error rate/volume).
- If an issue is likely customer-specific (e.g., client timeout misconfig, retry storm, SSO metadata mismatch), Support should follow runbook/KB first and only page if:
  - Mitigation requires platform change OR
  - Multiple customers / regions affected OR
  - Enterprise/Dedicated/Private with contractual SLA risk.
- SRE wants:
  - Update frequency expectations aligned with incident process (#incidents).
  - A way to measure the impact of policy changes (paging volume, MTTA/MTTR, false page rate).

Notes from Docs (Elliot)
- We need an explicit “safe-to-share” rubric.
- Anything that implies internal instability or security posture needs review before going public.
- Docs prefers issue pages follow a consistent template:
  - Symptoms, scope/applicability, how to confirm, workaround(s), what to collect, escalation trigger.

Notes from CS leadership (Jasmine/Rachel)
- Enterprise expectations:
  - After-hours coverage must be unambiguous by tier.
  - If we can’t commit to a time-to-resolution, we can commit to update cadence + time-to-mitigation targets.
- We need a standard comms tone: factual, time-stamped, avoid overpromising (“we believe” vs “confirmed”).

Known-issues sprint: initial candidates (from Support)
- Streaming disconnects + reconnect guidance (client patterns + timeouts, plus internal diagnostics).
- 429 throttling/quota misconfiguration (self-serve confusion; mitigate via better SDK messaging + docs).
- Dedicated latency spikes / noisy-neighbor suspicion (runbook refresh + alert tuning; mitigation levers).
- Private SSO/SAML failures after IdP changes (checklist + escalation boundary: Security vs Private Deployments).

OPEN QUESTIONS (need answers + owner)
1) Severity taxonomy: P0–P4 vs Sev0–Sev3 mapping
- Question: Are we going to keep both, or pick one canonical label?
- Proposal: Support uses P-level; SRE incident uses Sev-level; playbook explicitly maps them.
- Need: concrete mapping table + examples.
- Owner: Dev + Sean
- Due: end of week 1 (so SLA tables can be finalized)

2) Customer tier definitions (for SLA tables)
- Question: Do we treat “Private” and “Enterprise” as separate tiers or is enterprise a contract overlay that can apply to Hosted/Dedicated/Private?
- Impact: SLA language, after-hours coverage, escalation triggers.
- Owner: Rachel Kim + PM (PM-612)
- Stakeholders: Jasmine, Legal/CRO via Jordan Blake (loop-in as needed)

3) After-hours expectations
- Question: What does after-hours mean operationally?
  - “24/7 for P0 only” vs “24/7 for P0/P1 for enterprise/dedicated/private”
  - Which channel is staffed? (Pager? #incidents? Support inbox?)
- Proposal to evaluate:
  - Self-serve: business hours best-effort; after-hours only for confirmed multi-customer incidents.
  - Dedicated/Private/Enterprise: 24/7 for P0; P1 after-hours requires escalation approval criteria.
- Owners: Jasmine + Sean
- Constraint: paging hygiene; avoid turning all high-touch accounts into oncall pages.

4) “What constitutes an escalation?” thresholding
- Need explicit triggers per failure mode:
  - 5xx rate, timeout rate, streaming disconnect rate, 429 spike, Dedicated capacity shortfall, Private auth failures
- Question: define quantitative vs qualitative thresholds.
- Proposal: define “customer impact class” + “signal strength” (dashboards/alerts) + “repro/metadata completeness” as gating.
- Owner: Owen Phillips + Rafael Mendes

5) Status page vs customer thread comms alignment
- Question: At what point does Support post to status page vs keep comms 1:1?
- Need: clear rule for suspected widespread incidents vs single-account.
- Owner: Sean + Dev
- Related: status-page alignment doc in Confluence (existing)

6) “Safe-to-share” policy for known issues
- Question: When do we publish publicly?
  - If workaround is client-side and non-sensitive: likely yes.
  - If workaround reveals internal infra details or security posture: internal only.
- Need: a checklist and approvers.
- Owner: Elliot Price + PM (PM-613)
- Approvers: Security (Marcus Lin / Fiona McCarthy) for any auth/security-related content

7) Request ID and log retention constraints (esp. Private)
- Question: What can we ask customers to send? What is prohibited?
- Need: template text for Support to request logs safely; define “restricted handling” accounts.
- Owner: Dev + Security escalation owner (Marcus)

8) Jira required fields + automation
- Question: Which fields are mandatory before escalation/paging?
  - timestamps, request IDs, org/project, region, model, SDK version, error messages, sample curl, customer impact summary
- Need: enforce via templates + potential linting/incident-bot prompts.
- Owners: Owen + Miles (ENG-2842, ENG-2843)

Initial draft outline for Confluence pages (v2)
A) Escalation Playbook v2 — Overview (landing)
- Purpose + guiding principles
- Definitions: escalation vs incident, P-level vs Sev-level
- “How to use this playbook”
- Links to severity matrix, SLA tables, ownership map, comms templates, known issues

B) Severity matrix + triage criteria
- Table: P0–P4 w/ definitions
- Examples by failure mode:
  - Hosted 5xx/timeouts
  - Streaming disconnects
  - 429 throttling
  - Dedicated latency spikes/capacity
  - Private SSO/SAML, audit-log issues
- Triage checklist (what to collect, first 10 minutes)

C) Support + Engineering SLAs by tier
- First response SLA (Support)
- Engineering engagement SLA (ack + first meaningful update)
- Update frequency expectations
- Time-to-mitigation targets (where applicable)
- After-hours rules
- Escalation triggers by tier

D) Escalation paths + ownership map
- Component ownership (API gateway, scheduler, serving runtime, auth/RBAC, private installer, routing)
- “Who to page” and “who to loop in”
- Backup contacts + handoff rules
- When to route to Security vs Private Deployments vs Runtime vs SRE

E) Customer comms templates
- Investigation started
- Mitigation applied / workaround
- Monitoring
- RCA commitment
- Closure
- Tone + what not to promise
- Restricted account guidance

F) Support process: Jira ticket template + required fields
- Required fields list
- Linking rules: Slack threads, incidents, GitHub PRs, dashboards
- Example “good escalation” ticket

G) Known issues index + tagging scheme
- Tag taxonomy: Hosted/Dedicated/Private; region; model family; runtime version; SDK; safe-to-share
- Decision tree: when to use workaround vs escalate

Sprint plan (rough, will be mirrored into Linear ENG-2841)
Week 1 (Discovery + data pull)
- Pull top drivers + examples (SUP tickets) and map to failure modes
- Draft severity + SLA tables (Support + SRE)
- Owners: Priya (themes), Chris (reporting), Dev/Sean (policy)

Week 2 (Draft playbook + templates)
- Confluence pages created in draft state
- Comms templates v1
- Jira required fields list + template draft
- Owners: Dev + Elliot + Owen

Week 2–3 (Known-issues sprint execution)
- Publish 3–5 top known-issues pages w/ validated workarounds
- Ship at least 1–2 small fixes:
  - incident-bot workflow prompts
  - dashboard/runbook surfacing for streaming disconnects
  - SDK retry/backoff defaults or error messaging improvements
- Owners: Priya (KB validation), Miles (bot), Allison (obs standards), Alex/Monica/Ibrahim (SDK)

Week 4 (Rollout + training)
- Run Support training session (incl. scenarios)
- Announce policy changes in #announcements + pin Confluence links
- Start weekly metrics review cadence
- Owners: Dev + Elliot + Chris

Reviewer list (who needs to sign off / be consulted)
- Support: Dev Patel, Owen Phillips, Priya Shah
- CS leadership: Jasmine Liu, Rachel Kim, Liam O’Rourke (enterprise comms expectations)
- SRE/Oncall: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Miles Thornton, Tomáš Novák
- Docs: Elliot Price, Wei Chen (Hosted help), Kira Thompson (Dedicated/Private docs)
- DevEx/SDK: Alex Martinez, Monica Patel, Ibrahim Khan
- Product Ops: Chris Osei
- Product: (via PM-612/PM-613 owners)
- Security (as needed): Marcus Lin, Fiona McCarthy
- Private Deployments (as needed): Vivek Kulkarni

Action items (captured in kickoff)
- Dev: create Confluence space/page skeletons + share links for review (ETA: 2026-02-07)
- Sean/Rafael: propose paging thresholds + incident declaration criteria language (ETA: 2026-02-10)
- Elliot: propose known-issues page template + “safe-to-share” checklist (ETA: 2026-02-10)
- Priya: draft first 3 known-issues pages for validation (streaming disconnects, 429, dedicated latency spikes) (ETA: 2026-02-12)
- Owen: finalize “escalation required fields” list and map to Jira fields (ETA: 2026-02-11)
- Miles: confirm incident-bot changes scope + timeline; align with required fields (ENG-2843) (ETA: 2026-02-12)
- Chris: set up weekly reporting cadence proposal (MTTA/MTTR, ticket deflection, paging volume) (ETA: 2026-02-14)

Notes / Parking lot
- We should build a single ‘Escalation Intake’ snippet that Support can paste into Slack to reduce back-and-forth.
- Consider a lightweight “Escalation readiness score” (fields complete, request IDs present, repro exists, dashboards checked) before paging.
- Make sure we clearly distinguish:
  - client-side guidance (safe, public)
  - operational mitigations (may be internal-only)
  - product changes (eng tickets)

Changelog
